signal-amber.note: Campfire --spark under .dark. The system's entire emphasis budget; marks live state only.

caution-hay.note: Campfire --warning-500. Reversible-but-consequential actions, and every focus ring. 8.4:1 on slate-panel.

adopt-moss.note: Campfire --success-400. Additive and confirming actions. 6.5:1 on slate-panel.

destroy-coral.note: Campfire --danger-400. Irreversible or service-affecting actions, and error text. 5.0:1 on slate-panel.

listen-pine.note: Campfire --pine lifted 35% toward --ink; pine has no numbered ramp and its .dark value is 2.8:1. Passive/observational: auditioning, location, sparklines.

night-ground.note: Campfire --neutral-950. The page field AND the recessed fill inside controls — the same value doing both is what makes an input read as cut into a panel.

slate-panel.note: Campfire --neutral-900. Every card, table body, drawer and menu.

hairline.note: Campfire --neutral-700. Row separators and field dividers. Replaced an earlier token that resolved to the panel colour itself (1.00:1).

steel.note: Campfire --neutral-500. Two non-text jobs: the resting edge of every interactive control (3.1:1, clears WCAG 1.4.11), and decorative glyphs — carets, chevrons, the fader groove.

bright-ink.note: Campfire --neutral-50. Primary text and data. 12.4:1 on slate-panel.

cool-label.note: Campfire --neutral-300, reached past the semantic scale on purpose: the dark theme has no third text tier above 4.5:1, so labels and hints would otherwise be the same gray. 6.9:1.

quiet-hint.note: Campfire --neutral-400. Helper text, units, column headers, empty states. 4.6:1 — the dimmest tier that is still text.

position-unknown.note: A hit with no honest map position. Deliberately distinct from every service colour — uncertain geography must never look located.

shadow-ink.note: Depth only, 28-85% alpha: every shadow plus the drawer scrim. Never a surface colour.

overmap-plate.note: 70% behind aircraft callsign chips, where the ground is arbitrary map imagery.

wall-ground.note: Ambient canvas skin. Deliberately darker than Night Ground — an unlit room, not a panel.

art-ground.note: Outer stop of the art surface's radial ground.

art-ground-lift.note: Centre stop — the faint lift under the sediment field.

storm-tornado.note: NWS convention, externally mandated. Do not restyle toward the Kerchunk palette.

micro.purpose: Instrument legends: column headers, eyebrows, chips, badges, unit suffixes. Tracked 0.06em, usually uppercase.

caption.purpose: Interface chrome: buttons, nav, hints, card sub-headers.

dense.purpose: Table and list body, empty states, error text.

body.purpose: Prose, inputs, form labels. Paragraphs cap at 48rem (~52ch).

title.purpose: Card headers and the masthead brand.

lead.purpose: Emphasised inline values: system gauges, insight totals, the now-playing frequency.

display-sm.purpose: The live channel name in the admin hero.

display-lg.purpose: The drawer's frequency — the largest thing in the admin.

page-title.purpose: Admin page titles, one per page. Clamped to viewport width — off the fixed ramp on purpose.

kiosk-display.purpose: The kiosk's live channel name, read from across a room. Kiosk only.

shadows.name: floating-panel
shadows.purpose: The channel drawer sliding over the page.

shadows.name: over-map-card
shadows.purpose: Kiosk cards floating on the live map, where the background is arbitrary and the shadow is what keeps the card edge findable.

shadows.name: live-tag-glow
shadows.purpose: The system's only glow: the kiosk's live channel name. A glowing thing reads as 'on' from further away than a bright thing does.

motion.name: drawer-slide
motion.purpose: The channel drawer entering from the right. Quieted to 1ms under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: control-state
motion.purpose: Button border/colour/background feedback. Colour is information, so it survives prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: breathe
motion.purpose: The ACTIVE dot on the kiosk — the radio is receiving right now.

motion.name: sweep
motion.purpose: Idle scanning bar — the radio is working, not stuck.

motion.name: alert-pulse
motion.purpose: Weather alert card. Watch and warning tiers only; statement tier never pulses.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: Bottom tab bar, single-column forms, compact headers, triage actions move into the drawer.

breakpoints.name: tablet
breakpoints.purpose: Nav rail becomes a horizontal strip.

breakpoints.name: laptop
breakpoints.purpose: Stat tiles collapse from 4+1 to two columns.

narrative.overview:
Kerchunk is a radio that never sleeps, watched by one person who is usually doing something else. Every surface is built for that: a dark room, a glance from across it, and exactly one thing lit. At rest the whole interface is quiet gray on near-black — panels, rules, labels, and data all sit in a narrow neutral band. Emphasis is not distributed; it is spent.

That restraint is what makes the appliance readable at speed. The operator is not reading the screen — they are checking it, from a doorway, while the radio talks. So hierarchy is carried by size and by liveness, not by decoration. Cards are flat plates with hairline borders. Numbers are tabular so columns line up and a changing digit doesn't shift its neighbours. Labels are small, uppercase and tracked so they read as instrument legends rather than as prose.

The system takes its palette and its ramps from Campfire, the operator's own design system, and its type from a single face. It does not take its personality from hardware nostalgia: there are no bevels, no brushed metal, no fake screws. Instrument logic — legends, meters, consequence colour, tabular data — without instrument cosplay.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-only. There is no light theme and no theme switch; the use scene is a dim room and a wall-mounted panel.
One loud colour, spent on live state.
Flat plates, hairline rules, tonal layering; shadow only where something genuinely floats.
Tabular numerals everywhere a number can change.
Small tracked uppercase labels; large unadorned data.
Every surface legible from across a room or from a phone held at arm's length — never optimised for only one.

rules.name: The One Lit Thing Rule
rules.body: Signal Amber marks live state and nothing else. If two things on a screen are amber, one of them is wrong. Brand presence comes from restraint, not from coverage.

rules.name: The Dark-Value Rule
rules.body: Campfire's named expressive tokens (--flamingo, --sage, --pine, --golden-amber) carry a second, much darker value under .dark — the theme this app always runs in. Aliasing them for text or edges silently lands at 2.8–3.6:1. Take consequence colours from the numbered ramps (--danger-400, --success-400, --warning-500), which are theme-independent, and lift Pine toward --ink because it has no ramp.

rules.name: The Three-Tier Rule
rules.body: Text uses exactly three tiers — Bright Ink, Cool Label, Quiet Hint — and all three clear 4.5:1 on Slate Panel (12.4 / 6.9 / 4.6). There is no fourth, dimmer tier, because the dark ground does not have room for one. Anything dimmer than Quiet Hint is a glyph, not text.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Any number that can change while being looked at — frequency, temperature, CPU, hit count, clock, dB — is font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. A digit that changes width makes an instrument look unreliable.

rules.name: The Legend Rule
rules.body: Uppercase is for legends, never for reading. Tracked uppercase marks a label naming a value; it is never used for a sentence, a button that isn't a legend, or body copy.

rules.name: The Four-Decimal Rule
rules.body: Frequencies always render to four decimals (145.1300), never three. Scanner frequencies sit on a 12.5 kHz raster and three decimals misrepresents them.

rules.name: The One Scroll Rule
rules.body: A page has exactly one vertical scroll region. Tables are table-layout: fixed with declared column widths at every width, so they never scroll sideways and never need an inner scroll box. Sticky table headers stick against the page, not against a nested container.

rules.name: The Thumb Rule
rules.body: On coarse pointers every target is ≥44px (2.75rem). The only exemptions are glyphs whose surrounding cell or row is itself the larger target.

rules.name: The No-Glass Rule
rules.body: No backdrop-filter, no blur, no translucent-frosted surfaces. This is a thermal constraint first — blur over the animating WebGL map measured +6 °C on this hardware — and a visual one second. Where a card must sit over the map, raise the background opacity to 90–96% instead.

rules.name: The One Glow Rule
rules.body: Exactly one glow exists in the system: the amber text-shadow on the kiosk's live channel name. It is what makes the tag read as on rather than merely bright. Do not add a second.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Borders are 1px. A thicker coloured border on a card, list item, callout or alert is not part of this system — emphasis comes from ground tint, type size, or the accent colour of the text itself.

rules.name: The Ramp Rule
rules.body: Font size comes from a --t-* token, never a literal. Before adding a step, check whether an existing one does the job — the ramp replaced 32 ad-hoc values, five of which sat between 0.82 and 0.88rem and carried no distinction a reader could see. The only literals allowed are the two clamps and the two em values.

rules.name: The No-Pixels Rule
rules.body: Type is sized in rem or em, never px. Three px sizes had crept in (11, 13, 14) and silently ignored browser zoom and OS font-size settings — on an appliance read at arm's length and from across a room, that is the wrong thing to freeze.

rules.name: The Borrowed Palette Rule
rules.body: Depth inks, ambient canvas grounds and the NWS storm palette are part of the system but not interchangeable with it. Nothing else may borrow them, and the storm colours are never restyled toward the Kerchunk palette — an operator reading a tornado warning from across a room is relying on a colour they already know.

dos: Do spend Signal Amber on live state only — one lit thing per screen.
Do take consequence colours from Campfire's numbered ramps (--danger-400, --success-400, --warning-500), never from the named expressive tokens, which are darker under .dark.
Do give every interactive edge ≥3:1 against both its card and its own fill, and every text tier ≥4.5:1.
Do use font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on any number that can change while being watched.
Do keep frequencies at four decimals.
Do declare table column widths and use table-layout: fixed, so nothing scrolls sideways.
Do raise background opacity to 90–96% when a card must sit over the live map.
Do hit 44px targets on coarse pointers, exempting only glyphs whose row or cell is already the target.
Do edit the rule that already exists rather than restating it further down the stylesheet.
Do take every font size from a --t-* ramp token; the only literals are the two clamps and the two em-relative sizes.
donts: Don't use backdrop-filter, blur, or frosted glass anywhere. It is a measured thermal cost (+6 °C) and a visual anti-goal.
Don't add a coloured border-left/border-right thicker than 1px to a card, alert, list item or callout.
Don't add a second glow. The live channel tag owns the only one.
Don't drift toward a generic dark SaaS dashboard: purple-blue gradients, soft glow cards, decorative sparklines standing in for data.
Don't reach for skeuomorphic hardware texture — bevels, brushed metal, fake screws, drop-shadowed knobs.
Don't adopt a consumer scanner-app look: bright chrome, playful colour, phone-only layouts that lose the across-the-room read.
Don't introduce a fourth text tier dimmer than Quiet Hint; make it a glyph or make it brighter.
Don't use monospace as a signal of 'technical'. One face, tabular figures.
Don't invent a second card-header grammar, or a radius between 4px and 8px.
Don't repeat a Campfire token's hex as a var(--token, #hex) fallback; the token layer is always loaded, and a duplicated hex drifts silently.
Don't size type in px — it freezes out browser zoom and OS font-size settings.
Don't restyle the NWS storm palette toward the Kerchunk palette, and don't use a depth ink as a surface colour.
